fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"The Tower, The Bull, The Tarot","body":"Dylan Saccoccio builds the episode on a cluster of words he hears as one family: Welsh taru and Cornish taro for bull, Taurus the bull, the word for tower on the Marseille tarot card that he says is Italian rather than French, French Tours, Tyre, Thor, and Turms, the Etruscan Hermes. Ancient writers claimed the Tyrrhenians were named for the towers they built on high ground, which for him links Italy, Phoenicia and the Pelasgians. Chance Garton adds letter swaps that turn tor into Don the Lord, and both suggest the tarot itself may carry a bull and tower name."},{"title":"The Sun's Hidden Monogram","body":"A Cornish spelling of Jesu sends Dylan Saccoccio into the letters themselves. He reads the iota, an inverted H doing the work of a Greek eta, and a Latinized upsilon, and argues this is the monogram of Bacchus that later got read as the name of Jesus, sharing its first sounds with Jehovah. The three hash marks in the sun behind it he assigns to winter solstice, equinox and summer solstice, which is why Hermes is called thrice great. Chance Garton adds that if the letters hide Hu the god and esh the fire, then beings made in that image are hu-man."},{"title":"Corn, Horn, and the Mural Crown","body":"Chance Garton traces a chain through the consonants of corn, horn and crown to the radiance of the sun, the cornucopia and the spike of wheat held by Virgo. Philo of Byblos, quoting Sanchuniathon, says the Phoenician father of the gods, Dagon, takes his name from grain, and Chance pairs that with Granus, an epithet of Apollo, which with a G to K swap gives Kronos. Dylan Saccoccio calls it a career-best connection. He adds the mural crown of tower ramparts worn by Cybele, Rhea and Fortuna, while Chance offers the Irish cnoc, glossed as the hill of the sun."},{"title":"Letters Before The Pictures","body":"Both hosts reject the textbook order in which picture writing precedes the alphabet. Dylan Saccoccio notes that hieroglyphic spellings of names like Ptolemy and Alexander map neatly onto Greek and Latin letters, which he thinks only makes sense if letters came first and the pictures were a later layer of encoding, and he leans on Higgins to argue that Champollion's method can be bent to make anything mean anything. Chance Garton suspects writing began as a priestly secret that leaked to wealthy outsiders. Dylan points out that the Latin word for letters sits one letter from the Latin word for secret."},{"title":"Tanit And The Priestess Card","body":"The promised payoff is the High Priestess. Dylan Saccoccio sets the Phoenician goddess Tanit beside the card and matches her ankh-shaped cone body, bent arms, and headgear that he reads as crescent and ark at once, plus the tau cross of Terminus, god of boundaries. Chance Garton asks what a bow is called in Latin, and arcus, sitting next to arx for citadel, sends both men into delighted disbelief. Eros and his arrows follow, then Taweret, the hippopotamus goddess whose Greek name means water horse, the fish-tailed hippocamp, and Tanit spelled TNT, which Chance values at 650."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Taurus, the Tarot Tower card, Thor, Tours, and the Tyrrhenian Sea all share one ancient root. In Inner Whirled Episode 3, Chance Garton and Dylan Saccoccio trace the bull-Lord-Tower symbol back to a hidden Etruscan and Phoenician empire that left its fingerprints across Western language, mythology, and the tarot. This episode covers Etruscan and Celtic origins, the goddess Tanit and the tarot's High Priestess card, hornism and the protective meaning of bull horns, Apollo Granus and Kronos, Phoenician and Punic philology, Cornish and Welsh etymology, and astrotheology connecting the Pleiades, the dove, and the constellation Taurus.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: This episode covers Etruscan and Celtic origins, the goddess Tanit and the tarot's High Priestess card, hornism and the protective meaning of bull horns, Apollo Granus and Kronos, Phoenician and Punic philology, Cornish and Welsh etymology, and astrotheology connecting the Pleiades, the dove, and the constellation Taurus.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Our Lady, Britannia and Columbia", "body": "The members half opens with Dylan moving the deck to a section he labels Our Lady, where a Taweret image seems to carry a lion mane, a baboon is read as Thoth, and a mark under her hand is read as the Ichthys or the Othala rune. From there he argues that everybody has conceded Britannia comes from Minerva, noting that the boat carrying his ancestor Domenico Caesar to America bore that name. A Plymouth statue with her trident, her cross shield and her lion follows, and the thread runs on to Columbia as Venus and Lucifer."}, {"title": "The Sun Without Modern Instruments", "body": "A long tangent leaves the slides behind and asks what the sky looks like once inherited assumptions are stripped away. Dylan describes losing power across a whole block of his city and meeting a darkness he had never known, then points to an article he published that week suggesting the sun may be whatever powers this world from somewhere outside it. The firmament is compared to the dense saline layer on an ocean floor that submarines cannot pass. Without a real Earth radius, the argument goes, nobody ever measured a distance to the sun, so of course it looked like a god."}, {"title": "Hermes Hiding Inside Hermann", "body": "Chance brings in research from the occult Germany episode he is preparing. Arminius, whom the Germans call Hermann, is memorialized wearing a winged helmet, and the credentialed academic who wrote a book about him never noticed that the name is Hermes. The same research supplies the Irminsul, which Chance reads as the cross of a crucified savior long before Jesus Christ, and which Charlemagne had to come and destroy. Dylan answers that the letters of Italy were the basis of the Scandinavian runes, and that Alto Adige, where Italians speak German, shows there is no real separation at all."}, {"title": "Hornism and the Italian Emblems", "body": "Dylan turns horns into an argument. The Shardana who served Egypt wear them, and he reads Sardon as Sir Don, the lord, through the same sigma tau interchange that lets the Phoenician capital be spelled one way and said another. Horned Viking helmets he calls an invention with nothing behind it in the record. Then comes jettatura, the Italian evil eye, where iettare means both to throw and to jinx while tura carries the bull found in Taurus and toro. Horns in Italy always warded off evil, the exact reverse of what the modern priest class teaches."}, {"title": "Selvans and the Yinx", "body": "The two closing reveals land back to back. Dylan finishes his deck on Selvans, a name written on an Etruscan caduceus, which means savior in Cornish and stands behind Sylvanus and Pan, after quoting Lockyer to argue that heliology began in the plain need to know when to plow and reap. Chance then opens his own slides on the Yinx, the nymph daughter of Pan and Echo whose love charm was a spinning wheel with a wryneck bird, and carries her through Hecate's eight spoked wheel to the Hunger Games mockingjay and finally to the dove."}]
